alex (cust-eng): Hey team — our Private deploy in customer VPC is failing to pull model artifacts and also pip installs are timing out. Errors show up as TLS handshake failures and 401s when the runtime tries to /oauth/token. We think outbound egress is restricted.
erin (support): Thanks Alex — can you paste the exact curl / logs you see when hitting the endpoints? Also, which outbound egress policy is in place (domain-only, IP ranges, proxy with TLS inspection)?
alex (cust-eng): Repro steps: deploy a test inference job -> runtime tries to fetch model from model registry -> fails. Quick curl from a bastion: `curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/registry/v1/models/my-model/manifest` output: 
```
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to models.redwood.ai (10.0.0.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL: TLS: Incoming alert: Handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```
Also runtime logs show: `AuthClient: POST https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token -> 401` (no body). We do have an outbound proxy that does MITM TLS cert re-signing.
erin (support): That MITM/TLS inspection is likely causing the handshake/unknown CA. Redwood runtime verifies cert chain for our auth and model registry endpoints. For Private deployments we recommend either: 1) bypass TLS inspection/proxy for Redwood domains, or 2) install the corporate CA into the container runtime's truststore and ensure the signing cert is trusted for outbound connections.
For immediate unblock, please allow outbound TLS (443) to the domains below without interception. Also allow package registry endpoints used during bootstrap. Minimal domains to allow (TLS port 443):
```
- auth.redwood.ai
- models.redwood.ai
- registry.redwood.ai
- artifacts.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com
- s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-models
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- registry.npmjs.org
- registry.yarnpkg.com
- raw.githubusercontent.com
- packages.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- api.segment.com
- api.datadoghq.com
- backup.redwood.ai
```
erin (support): If your allowlist only supports IP ranges, we can provide the current egress CIDRs used by our hosted control plane and CDN. Note these may change if we add capacity; we recommend domain+/TLS bypass where possible.
alex (cust-eng): Thanks — is there a specific port list or headers required? We currently only allow 443 and 80; we don't want to open any extra ports.
erin (support): 443 is sufficient for everything we need. For package installs: npm/pip all use 443. For S3 presigned URLs the client will use 443. If you have an outbound web proxy, ensure CONNECT tunneling is allowed for these hostnames (no certificate re-signing).
Also watch for firewall rules that do SNI-based filtering — ensure the SNI matches those hostnames and not an IP. If you're using IP-based allowlist, include our published CIDRs and CloudFront/ CDN edge ranges — I'll loop infra-oncall to provide them.
infra-oncall: Looping in — Erin, Alex: we can provide a snapshot of current CIDRs and CDN hostnames. Note: our model artifact hosting is served via multiple S3 buckets and CloudFront distributions. Please allow these hostnames (example list):
```
- d111.cloudfront.net (CloudFront edges for artifacts)
- artifacts-redwood.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
- s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
- models-cdn.redwood.ai
```
infra-oncall: We'll also email the exact CIDR list for our control plane: `34.200.112.0/20, 54.204.0.0/16` (note: these are example ranges — using domain allowlist is preferred). We'll send a signed manifest with the ranges and last-updated timestamp so you can automate sync.
alex (cust-eng): Understood. One more oddity — runtime reports `401` from /oauth/token but curl gets 200 when run from my laptop. Could that be a client cert/kms issue?
erin (support): If TLS inspection is removed and you still get 401, verify the following: 1) system time on the hosts (JWT time skew can cause 401), 2) your env has the correct client credentials / service account secrets mounted, 3) proxy not dropping Authorization headers. Also check that your egress NAT (if using SNAT) isn't translating source IP to something we block for that tenant — we can check logs if you send the request-id from the runtime logs.
alex (cust-eng): Got the request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e. Also time was off on one node by ~15min, fixing now.
erin (support): Great — once time and TLS bypass are fixed, try the following test from the bastion: 
```
# test auth token fetch
curl -v -X POST "https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"client_id":"<id>","client_secret":"<secret>","grant_type":"client_credentials"}'
# test model manifest
curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/registry/v1/models/my-model/manifest
```
alex (cust-eng): Running tests now. If this works I'll report back. Thanks for the checklist.
deploy-bot: deployment/rdw-private-123 status changed to FAILED — see logs: `fetch artifact failed: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority`
alex (cust-eng): Re-ran curl after adding corporate CA to container truststore -> auth token POST now returns 200, model manifest fetch returns 200, runtime job started successfully. Looks like MITM was the root cause. We'll still request the domain allowlist change so future nodes don't need special CA installs.
erin (support): Thanks for confirming. I'll open an internal ticket to provide the formal allowlist and the signed CIDR manifest for your security team. Ticket: SUP-8421. We'll also include a short doc on TLS inspection impacts for Private deployments.
infra-oncall: Sent email with CIDRs and edge hostnames. Also included automation instructions for syncing the list via our signed JSON at https://control.redwood.ai/egress-cidrs.json (GET, 443).
alex (cust-eng): Received. Closing on our side once security approves. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
